examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2C Solution Architect Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam page covers B2C solution design across commerce, customer engagement and service. Expect to reason about how the parts of a customer journey fit together.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Scenario-based choices: expect questions that test when to use B2C Commerce, Multi-Cloud, or Solution Design.
Hands-on context matters: candidates who have configured or supported B2C Commerce in a real org are better prepared than candidates who only memorize notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the published objectives to build a study checklist. Practice tracing customer needs across commerce, marketing, service and order handling, then review why each design choice fits.

examFormat.heading: B2C Solution Architect Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The B2C Solution Architect exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios describe a retailer’s goal and ask which design best supports the customer journey, operations or non-functional needs.
bestWayToPass: Trace the shopping journey: Map how a customer discovers products, checks out, and gets help after the sale. Note which cloud owns each step.
Design the commerce and order flow: Review catalogs, promotions, carts, order capture, fulfillment routing, returns, and refunds as one connected solution.
Plan for peak shopping periods: Use scale, caching, and recovery plans to support traffic spikes, global storefronts, and service uptime.
Coordinate releases across clouds: Plan changes to Commerce, Marketing Cloud, and Salesforce metadata together, and identify where testing or rollback is needed.

certificationCard.description: This exam page reviews B2C solution architecture across Commerce Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Service Cloud and order management. Use the exam details shown on the card to plan your preparation. The exam is 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Discovery and Customer Success (27%) and Data Models and Management (25%).

keyConcepts.h2: B2C Solution Architect: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: B2C Solution Design
blocks.body: Start with the customer journey and business goals. Map each step to the Salesforce product or service that supports it, and document the boundaries between systems.

blocks.heading: Multi-Cloud Data Flow
blocks.body: Decide which system owns each customer or order record and how updates move between products. Keep identity matching, consent and error handling in the design.

blocks.heading: Customer Identity
blocks.body: Shoppers may browse anonymously before creating an account. Plan how the solution recognizes a returning customer, handles duplicate profiles and respects consent.

blocks.heading: Orders and Fulfillment
blocks.body: Commerce captures the purchase. Order-management and fulfillment processes handle what happens next, such as routing, delivery, returns and status updates.

blocks.heading: Scale and Resilience
blocks.body: Plan for busy shopping periods, response time, recovery and safe releases. Choose caching and scaling approaches that fit the actual traffic and service requirements.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce B2C Solution Architect Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Map each requirement to the customer journey and the Salesforce products that support it.

blocks.heading: Follow the customer journey
blocks.body: Identify what the shopper is doing, which system owns the step and what information the next step needs.

blocks.heading: Check identity and data ownership
blocks.body: Look for duplicate profiles, consent rules and unclear ownership between connected clouds.

blocks.heading: Design for order completion
blocks.body: Follow the order through fulfillment and customer support, including failure and return paths.

blocks.heading: Use constraints to compare options
blocks.body: Choose a design that meets the stated scale, availability, mobile and release needs without adding unrelated components.

sampleQuestions.question: A retailer wants one design that ties its consumer storefront to supporting Salesforce services. What should the architect lead?
options: A list of storefront page changes only
A service-desk process without commerce data
A product catalogue migration with no customer journey
sampleQuestions.explanation: The architect should shape the end-to-end customer solution across the clouds the business needs, rather than focus on one isolated component.
whyWrong: A list of storefront page changes only does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.
A service-desk process without commerce data does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.
A product catalogue migration with no customer journey does not fit because it addresses a different need than A customer-focused design across the relevant Salesforce clouds.

sampleQuestions.question: A team is planning a direct-to-consumer online store. What does B2C mean?
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2C means Business-to-Consumer: a business sells products or services directly to consumers.
whyWrong: Business-to-Channel does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.
Brand-to-Customer does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.
Buyer-to-Commerce does not fit because it addresses a different need than Business-to-Consumer.

sampleQuestions.question: A company needs a consumer storefront, campaign engagement and customer support. Which Salesforce capabilities best match those needs?
options: Experience Cloud and Revenue Cloud only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Commerce supports the storefront, Marketing Cloud supports customer engagement, and Service Cloud supports service.
whyWrong: Sales Cloud, Tableau and Slack does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.
Service Cloud and Heroku alone does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.
Experience Cloud and Revenue Cloud only does not fit because it addresses a different need than B2C Commerce, Marketing Cloud and Service Cloud.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer journey spans shopping, marketing messages and post-purchase support. What does a multi-cloud design require?
options: Keeping each cloud isolated from the others
Using one product for every business process
Sending all customer data into a spreadsheet
Coordinate data and interactions across clouds
sampleQuestions.explanation: A multi-cloud solution coordinates the data and customer experience across the products used in the journey.
whyWrong: Keeping each cloud isolated from the others does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.
Using one product for every business process does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.
Sending all customer data into a spreadsheet does not fit because it addresses a different need than Coordinating data and interactions across the products involved.

sampleQuestions.question: Who is most likely to pursue a B2C Solution Architect role?
options: Campaign writers focused only on creative copy
Retail store associates with no platform responsibilities
Product designers focused only on visual assets
sampleQuestions.explanation: The role suits architects and senior consultants who design B2C solutions across business and Salesforce requirements.
whyWrong: Campaign writers focused only on creative copy does not fit because it addresses a different need than Architects and senior consultants designing consumer commerce solutions.
Retail store associates with no platform responsibilities does not fit because it addresses a different need than Architects and senior consultants designing consumer commerce solutions.
Product designers focused only on visual assets does not fit because it addresses a different need than Architects and senior consultants designing consumer commerce solutions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a B2C Commerce storefront give a retailer?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The storefront is the consumer-facing channel where shoppers browse and purchase.
whyWrong: A partner-only account portal does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.
A field-service dispatch console does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.
A back-office finance ledger does not fit because it addresses a different need than A consumer-facing online shopping experience.

sampleQuestions.question: A retailer wants Commerce shopping activity to inform Marketing Cloud engagement. Which integration should it evaluate?
options: A Tableau extract with no customer linkage
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Commerce and Marketing Cloud integration can share relevant commerce data for marketing use cases; the exact connector and design depend on the implementation.
whyWrong: A Service Cloud case queue does not fit because it addresses a different need than The Commerce-to-Marketing Cloud integration.
A Slack workspace connection does not fit because it addresses a different need than The Commerce-to-Marketing Cloud integration.
A Tableau extract with no customer linkage does not fit because it addresses a different need than The Commerce-to-Marketing Cloud integration.

sampleQuestions.question: A brand wants to build its own web or mobile interface while using commerce services behind it. Which approach fits?
options: A fixed storefront theme with no external interface
A single server-rendered page tied to the commerce UI
A monolithic application with no commerce APIs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Headless commerce separates the presentation layer from commerce services exposed through APIs.
whyWrong: A fixed storefront theme with no external interface does not fit because it addresses a different need than Headless commerce using APIs and a separate front end.
A single server-rendered page tied to the commerce UI does not fit because it addresses a different need than Headless commerce using APIs and a separate front end.
A monolithic application with no commerce APIs does not fit because it addresses a different need than Headless commerce using APIs and a separate front end.

sampleQuestions.question: A retailer wants recommendations on product pages based on shopper context. Which capability should it consider?
options: A static product list with no shopper signals
A manual spreadsheet sent to shoppers
sampleQuestions.explanation: Personalization and recommendation capabilities can tailor product suggestions using available shopper context and configured rules.
whyWrong: A static product list with no shopper signals does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.
A service case assignment rule does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.
A manual spreadsheet sent to shoppers does not fit because it addresses a different need than Personalization and recommendation features.

sampleQuestions.question: After checkout, a retailer needs to coordinate fulfillment and keep order status visible. Which integration area matters?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Post-purchase order fulfillment supports post-purchase processing such as fulfillment and order status updates.
whyWrong: Storefront page analytics does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.
Marketing email templates does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.
Product image storage does not fit because it addresses a different need than Order Management integration.

sampleQuestions.question: What should an architect check when several Salesforce clouds share customer data?
options: Whether each cloud can use a different identity for the same person
Whether the customer profile can be omitted from the design
Whether all customer interactions can be moved to one report
sampleQuestions.explanation: A multi-cloud architecture needs clear data flows, identity matching and a consistent customer experience.
whyWrong: Whether each cloud can use a different identity for the same person does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.
Whether the customer profile can be omitted from the design does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.
Whether all customer interactions can be moved to one report does not fit because it addresses a different need than How data flows, identity is matched and experiences remain consistent.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the architect’s role in a B2C Commerce program?
options: Own only the service team’s case queue
sampleQuestions.explanation: The architect aligns the solution across Commerce and the other products required to meet the customer and business needs.
whyWrong: Write every storefront component alone does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.
Manage only the campaign calendar does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.
Own only the service team’s case queue does not fit because it addresses a different need than Guide the end-to-end design across commerce and related services.

sampleQuestions.question: A retailer expects seasonal traffic spikes and does not want to manage storefront servers. Which deployment model fits?
options: A single on-premises server sized for average traffic
A fixed local instance with no scale plan
A desktop application installed for each shopper
sampleQuestions.explanation: A cloud-hosted service avoids customer-managed storefront servers and supports scale according to the service design and plan.
whyWrong: A single on-premises server sized for average traffic does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.
A fixed local instance with no scale plan does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.
A desktop application installed for each shopper does not fit because it addresses a different need than A cloud-hosted commerce service sized for variable demand.

sampleQuestions.question: A shopper needs help with an order after purchase. Which Salesforce capability is most relevant?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Cloud supports customer service workflows, including cases and order-related support.
whyWrong: Marketing Cloud audience segmentation does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.
Commerce product catalogue management does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.
Tableau dashboard authoring does not fit because it addresses a different need than Service Cloud case and customer support.

sampleQuestions.question: Which design principle should guide a consumer commerce solution?
options: Optimize internal reporting before customer needs
Build desktop pages first and defer mobile behavior
Treat each cloud as a separate customer experience
sampleQuestions.explanation: A B2C solution should follow the customer journey and account for performance and mobile use.
whyWrong: Optimize internal reporting before customer needs does not fit because it addresses a different need than Align the journey with performance and mobile use.
Build desktop pages first and defer mobile behavior does not fit because it addresses a different need than Align the journey with performance and mobile use.
Treat each cloud as a separate customer experience does not fit because it addresses a different need than Align the journey with performance and mobile use.
